scope: Primary-source desk research; no outreach, app installation, audio listening, language identification by ear, or shared-content edits.

findings.citation: Roland Hardenberg, Children of the Earth Goddess: Society, Marriage, and Sacrifice in the Highlands of Odisha (De Gruyter, 2018), section1.1, printedp3/PDFpage29.
findings.locator: PDF zero-based28; extractedlines536–563. Copyright page PDF4 verifies2018.
findings.claim_ready: Roland Hardenberg records Kuang Kata as a name Dongria people use for their language.
findings.context: An ethnographer’s attributed observation, useful beside catalogue classifications.
limits: Do not imply every contemporary speaker uses this name.
Footnote4 on the same page questions treating Kui and Kuwi as separate languages; author explicitly says he is not a linguist. Do not use that opinion to erase the existing CIIL distinction.
No wordlist, translation, dialect boundaries or numerical mutual-intelligibility estimate derived.

findings.citation: Glottolog5.3 DongriaKuvi and Kuvi entries, inspected8November2026.
findings.locator: Dongria page heading Dialect:DongriaKuvi; glottocode dong1300. Kuvi page heading SpokenL1Language:Kuvi, ISO639-3kxv.
findings.claim_ready: Glottolog5.3 lists a dialect entry named Dongria Kuvi, identified by dong1300; its Kuvi language entry is kuvi1243, with ISO code kxv.
limits: Catalogue labels do not establish the language of an individual recording or speaker.
Do not assign Dongria Kuvi a separate ISO language code.
JSON endpoint inaccessible; classificationtree not used to add further subgrouping.
Avoid generic endangered assertion: Kuvi page has not-endangered AES heading and separate at-risk source comment; these should not be flattened into a local assessment.

findings.citation: Kuvi Dictionary, developer listing Dictionary App Man; developerdetails KalaamMediaLtd; updated20April2026.
findings.locator: About this app; indexed languages tagline; Updated on.
findings.claim_ready: The Kuvi Dictionary Android listing describes an Andhra Pradesh variety of Kuvi and indexes in Telugu, English and Hindi. Its maintainers present it as a revisable community draft arising from an Education Department multilingual-education effort involving ITDAs.
limits: The collaboration and community approval are developer claims, not an independently inspected approval record.
Not a Dongria-specific Niyamgiri dictionary; do not transfer entries to local speech without comparison.
App not installed; entries, pronunciation audio, entrycount, writing-system details and contributor credits inside app unverified.
No connection to O Foundation established.
No government classroom deployment or learning outcome established.
Free access does not establish an open licence for reproducing dictionary text/audio/screenshots.

findings.locator: Official page OpenSpeaksArchives table, tools and framework; Meta phase1 Languagesandpeople and OpinoGomango testimony.
findings.claim_ready: O Foundation’s OpenSpeaks connects community language documenters with recording, archiving and subtitling resources. Its published regional work names Opino Gomango with Sora, Juray, Juang and Gorum documentation.
findings.use: A regional example and resource lead, not evidence of an existing DongriaKuvi archive.
limits: Checked organizationpage, archiveoverview, phase1/phase2 pages and Commonscategory; no verified DongriaKuvi recordingcollection located. This is bounded search, not proof none exists.
Odia voice corpus is Odia, not Kuvi.
Do not equate Sora/Juray/Juang/Gorum with Kuvi because the network works in Odisha.
Do not treat planned language documentation as completed work.
No partnership, endorsement, reviewer availability or outreach inferred.

findings.locator: OpenSpeaksTools and Frameworkandresearch sections; toolkit metadata/transcription sections.
findings.claim_ready: OpenSpeaks publishes tools for subtitles, recording metadata and consent documentation, together with a framework for describing and citing oral knowledge.
limits: Tools not tested here. Tool availability is not evidence of a Kuvi-specific speech model, automatic reliable translation or speaker validation.
Keep practical tool detail in resource box or KB unless needed by chapter narrative.
